Container.Name: NextDash
Container.DonateText: Find NextDash useful? Consider supporting the project.
Container.Overview:
NextDash is a lightweight, self-hosted bookmark dashboard that features a minimalist, keyboard-driven interface with extensive customization options, making it the perfect personal dashboard for power users. Based on the excellent ThinkDashboard.
Key features: • Keyboard-driven navigation for fast access to all your bookmarks, and a search that answers sums such as 15% of 240 • Extensive theme and layout customization, with a theme studio beside the dashboard, a theme editor and 285 backdrops drawn in the themes' colours • Inbox to collect new links fast: triage them, or keep them under Bookmarks → Unsorted and file whole groups later • Bookmarks view with Health built in: finds broken, stale and duplicate links, with uptime monitoring and downtime alerts • Network checks on a bookmark: TCP, Ping, DNS, TLS, HTTP and JSON on a schedule or once, with the result in the Tests tab, in the bell and on the dashboard. Ping needs ICMP; if it is blocked nextDash falls back to TCP and says so. To allow it, add --sysctl net.ipv4.ping_group_range="0 2147483647" to Extra Parameters (with Host networking set the sysctl on the Unraid host instead) • Edit mode: change categories, widgets and pages right on the dashboard, and put a widget on every page with one switch • A notifications bell: questions, notices and tips wait there, with their age, instead of popping up over your work • A checkup and a weekly digest that tell you what needs attention • Watch feeds: follow the RSS, Atom or JSON Feed of sites you choose, with news on the bookmark, in its preview card and in a news window • An assistant you ask in plain words, on Claude, OpenAI or a server of your own: it looks things up and changes nothing by itself • Video bookmarks marked in the list, and played in the hover card without leaving the dashboard • Widgets beside your bookmarks: 63 built-in kinds (tabs, clock, countdown, uptime, feeds, weather, disks, containers and more) plus a Custom widget for any JSON API • Your media stack on the dashboard: Jellyfin, Sonarr, Radarr, Seerr, qBittorrent and SABnzbd, with the posters from your own library, and your Immich photos as a frame, a slideshow, albums, people and a server status, and Jellystat, Bazarr and Prowlarr for who watched what, missing subtitles and how your indexers are doing • Finds the web apps in your Docker containers and offers them as bookmarks, with an icon and a status check (needs the Docker socket below), and up to four more Docker hosts as tabs in the Containers view • Glances on the dashboard: a page for the hosts you run Glances on, with processes, containers, graphs and incidents, and a widget for one host • Your Unraid server on the dashboard: seven widgets for the array, parity, shares, VMs, the UPS and notifications, with alerts • Web search in the search panel through your own SearXNG or the Brave Search API • Six interface languages: English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish and Chinese • Lightweight and fast, no heavy dependencies • Actively maintained with regular releases
Links: • Website: https://www.nextdash.cc • Source code and releases: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash • Changelog: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash/releases • Devlog / release updates: https://www.nextdash.cc/news • Also available on GHCR: ghcr.io/jordibrouwer/nextdash:latest • User manual: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash/blob/main/MANUAL.md
The host widgets (Processor, Memory, Disks, Containers) are off until you fill in the optional paths and variables below — they are hidden under Show more settings. Section 16.4 of the manual explains what each one reads.
Support: open an issue on GitHub via the Support link above. Bug reports and feature requests are welcome.
Container.Changes:
### v1.30.0 (2026-11-16) - Containers: up to four more Docker hosts, each as a tab above the list, read-only until you allow actions - Widgets: five Immich widgets (photos, slideshow, albums, people, status) and a bell row for failed Immich jobs - Widgets: a widget can show on every page, as an ordinary copy you move and resize per page - Bookmarks: a link dragged in from another window onto a category opens the bookmark form filled in - Phone: a Watch feeds switch in More - Themes: three more Christmas themes, Snow Globe, Paper Advent and Nutcracker Theatre
### v1.29.2 (2026-11-15) - Monitoring: network checks draw their response time, a small line per check and a 24 hour, 7 day or 30 day chart in the Tests tab - Bookmarks: a suggested name loses a login word or the site's own name, with an arrow to bring the page's own title back - Digest: the weekly digest opens with the week in a few plain sentences - Feeds: the news badge stays until the news is read, and the news window is an hour by default - Inbox: rows that load late still rise in
### v1.29.1 (2026-11-14) - Phone: search opens at once and keeps the tab bar under it, which lifts above the keyboard - Phone: RSS headlines open a preview sheet on a touch screen, with buttons to open the article - Phone: the Inbox selects are tall enough on an iPhone
### v1.29.0 (2026-11-13) - Phone: a tab bar with Home, Search, Inbox, Status and More; Status lists every monitored bookmark and pauses notifications for an hour or until tomorrow morning - Phone: two start screens, search first or status first, chosen per device - Phone: a compact search sheet, forms made for a thumb, an Inbox made for a thumb, and a press and hold menu on bookmarks - Feeds: adding a feed fetches its ten newest posts and opens the news popover on its row, on desktop and phone - Layout: a block can show on desktop only or on the phone only, from the edit panel, the block menus and Config → Structure
### v1.28.3 (2026-11-12) - Themes: the eight new theme groups also dress Bookmarks, Inbox, Containers, Glances, Tags and Config, not only the dashboard - Themes: the pane of every view is filled like a dashboard column, with the same opacity, in all 440 themes

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the NextDash web interface

Config.Name: AppData
Config.Description: Persistent storage path for NextDash data (bookmarks, settings)

Config.Name: Write token
Config.Description: Optional. Require this token in the X-NextDash-Token header on every write. Leave empty for an open instance on a trusted network.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Optional. Addresses and CIDR ranges whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed, comma-separated — set this if nextDash sits behind a reverse proxy, so rate limits count per visitor instead of per proxy. Left empty the header is ignored.

Config.Name: Allowed hosts
Config.Description: Optional. Only with a write token: public host names the dashboard may be opened by, comma-separated (*.example.com allowed, * turns the check off). IP addresses, localhost and private names (.local, .lan) always work. Needed when you open nextDash by your own domain.

Config.Name: Host proc
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the host /proc here for the Processor and Memory widgets. Host path: /proc

Config.Name: Host proc variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /host/proc once the mount above is filled in.

Config.Name: Host disks
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the array here for the Disks widget. Host path: /mnt — then name /mnt/user or /mnt/cache in the widget.

Config.Name: Host root variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /host/root once the disks mount above is filled in.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: Optional. Mount the Docker socket here for the Containers widget. Host path: /var/run/docker.sock — read-only still exposes the daemon's whole read API, so use a socket proxy if that is too much.

Config.Name: Docker socket variable
Config.Description: Optional. Set to /var/run/docker.sock once the socket mount above is filled in. Unset, the Containers widget is hidden.

Config.Name: Docker actions
Config.Description: Optional. 1 lets the Containers view start, stop, update and remove containers; 0 keeps it read-only. A writable socket is root on the host, so set a write token as well.

Config.Name: Run as root
Config.Description: Optional. 1 keeps nextDash running as root, needed only when the Docker socket belongs to root's group (gid 0). Unraid's socket belongs to the docker group (gid 281), so leave this at 0 here.
